safety.title: Crash test safety
safety.unavailable: Safety ratings aren't available right now.
safety.none: No NHTSA rating found — this US-market database rarely covers EU/JDM-spec or Soviet-era vehicles.
safety.coverageNhtsa: Covers vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year. Only reliably covers MY2011 onward (NHTSA's current combined 5-star program) — older model years used different, non-comparable test criteria.
safety.source: Source: NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings (USA) — matched by make/model/year, US-spec trims only.
safety.euroncapNone: No Euro NCAP rating found for this make/model.
safety.coverageEuroncap: Covers EU-spec vehicles Euro NCAP actually tested, 2017 onward. A rating expires 6 years after publication (shown as "other tested generations" past that point).
safety.euroncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.euroncapExpired: This rating has expired (Euro NCAP ratings are valid for 6 years from publication).
safety.euroncapSource: Source: Euro NCAP — matched by make/model, EU-spec vehicles.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: Euro NCAP's overall safety rating for this tested variant.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoAdultOccupant: Adult Occupant: how well the structure and restraints protect adult occupants in a crash.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoChildOccupant: Child Occupant: protection for children in the car's own child seats, plus how easy it is to fit compatible child seats.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoVulnerableRoad: Vulnerable Road Users: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car, and how well its systems detect them.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyAssist: Safety Assist: how much standard-fit tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, speed limiting) helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyPack: Safety Pack: results for an optional equipment package — the base/Standard trim may score differently.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoExpiry: Ratings expire after 6 years — Euro NCAP's test protocol gets stricter over time, so an old 5-star rating isn't directly comparable to a new one.
safety.jncapNone: No JNCAP rating found for this make/model — this Japan-domestic database only covers vehicles NASVA actually tested.
safety.coverageJncap: Covers JDM-domestic vehicles NASVA actually tested, 2003 onward (with real gaps: no 2004-2006 or 2008).
safety.jncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.jncapSource: Source: JNCAP (Japan, NASVA) — matched by make/model, JDM-domestic vehicles.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: JNCAP's overall safety rating for this tested vehicle.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoPreventive: Preventive safety: how well the car's active-safety tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, headlights) helps avoid a crash — graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoCollision: Collision safety: occupant and pedestrian protection in frontal, side, and whiplash tests — graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoEmergencyCall: Emergency call system: whether the car automatically alerts emergency services after a serious crash, and how advanced that system is.
safety.cncapNone: No C-NCAP rating found for this make/model — this China-market database only covers vehicles CATARC actually tested.
safety.coverageCncap: Covers China-market vehicles CATARC actually tested, 2006 onward.
safety.cncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.cncapSource: Source: C-NCAP (China, CATARC) — matched by make/model, China-market vehicles.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoUnit: C-NCAP has no star rating — scores before 2018 are raw points with no fixed maximum, and scores from 2018 onward are a clean percentage; the two are never directly comparable.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoOccupant: Occupant protection: how well the structure and restraints protect occupants in a crash.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoVru: Pedestrian/VRU protection: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.cncapRatingsInfoActiveSafety: Active safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.kncapNone: No KNCAP rating found for this make/model — this Korea-market database only covers vehicles KNCAP actually tested.
safety.coverageKncap: Covers Korea-market vehicles KNCAP actually tested, 2021 onward — an older historical corpus exists but isn't in this database yet.
safety.kncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.kncapSource: Source: KNCAP (Korea, MOLIT/KoROAD) — matched by make/model, Korea-market vehicles, 2021 onward only.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoClass: Class (1-5): KNCAP's overall safety tier for this tested vehicle — 1 is the best.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoCrash: Crash safety: occupant protection in frontal, side, and pole-impact tests.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoPedestrian: Pedestrian safety: protection for pedestrians struck by the car.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoAccident: Accident-prevention safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.iihsNone: No IIHS rating found for this make/model — this US-market database only covers vehicles IIHS actually tested.
safety.coverageIihs: Covers US-market vehicles IIHS actually tested, model year 1994 onward.
safety.iihsNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year.
safety.iihsSource: Source: IIHS (US, insurance-industry-funded) — matched by make/model, US-market vehicles, model year 1994 onward only.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoScale: Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor: IIHS's crashworthiness scale across small-overlap front, moderate-overlap front, side, and headlight tests.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoFcp: Front crash prevention: Superior/Advanced/Basic on older tests, or Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor on newer ones — how well standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoAward: Top Safety Pick / Top Safety Pick+: IIHS's annual award for vehicles meeting its highest combined standards that model year.
safety.coverageInfoIntro: All six sources are supplementary, best-effort matches — none of them guarantees a result for every car, so always check the vehicle's actual specification.
safety.coverageInfoEuroNcapBody: Tests EU-spec cars — the vast majority of Ukraine's registered fleet by brand — but only specific tested trims and generations, not every model or year. A rating only shows up when Euro NCAP actually tested that make/model.
safety.brandsInfoIntro: NHTSA only tests vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year — not every model or year of a covered brand has a rating on file.
safety.brandsInfoDiscontinued: Discontinued in the US (older model years only)
safety.brandsInfoUncovered: Never sold in the US — no rating will ever exist, e.g.
safety.coverageInfoJncapBody: Tests JDM-domestic cars — models never exported to the EU or US, like the Toyota Alphard/Crown/Mark X or Nissan Skyline/Cedric/Elgrand. Only vehicles NASVA actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoCncapBody: Tests China-market cars — the BYD/Geely/Chery/Zeekr/Haval fleet Ukraine grey-imports in volume — under their China-spec names, translated here from CATARC's own Chinese-language results. Only vehicles CATARC actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoKncapBody: Tests Korea-domestic cars — Hyundai/Kia/Genesis/KGM EVs and other Korea-only models — under their Korean names, translated here from KNCAP's own results. Only covers 2021 onward, and only vehicles KNCAP actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoIihsBody: Tests the same US-spec fleet NHTSA does, but on a different methodology (Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor across small-overlap, side, and crash-prevention tests, plus Top Safety Pick awards) — a car can rate well on one scale and not the other. Only vehicles IIHS actually tested have a rating.
safety.ratingsInfoStars: 1–5 stars, more stars = safer. "Not Rated" means NHTSA never tested that specific trim.
safety.ratingsInfoOverall: Overall: a combined score across all frontal, side, and rollover tests below.
safety.ratingsInfoFront: Front: driver/passenger protection in a 35 mph frontal crash into a fixed barrier.
safety.ratingsInfoSide: Side: occupant protection in a 38 mph side impact, plus a separate side pole impact test.
safety.ratingsInfoAverage: Average: when a make/model/year has several tested trims (body style, drivetrain), this is the mean across all of them, shown above the individual breakdown.
safety.ratingsInfoRollover: Rollover: risk of a rollover in a single-vehicle loss-of-control event — more stars = lower risk.
safety.ratingsInfoSidePole: Side pole: a separate, more severe side-impact test against a narrow pole (like a tree or post).
safety.ratingsInfoRolloverRisk: Rollover risk %: the actual estimated probability of a rollover, behind the star rating — plus the dynamic test result (e.g. "No Tip") from a real avoidance-maneuver test.
safety.ratingsInfoEquipment: ESC/FCW/LDW: whether stability control, forward-collision warning, and lane-departure warning came standard, optional, or weren't offered on this trim.
safety.ratingsInfoCombinedSideBarrier: Side barrier (combined): an older/secondary side-impact sub-score alongside the main Side and Side pole ratings above.
safety.ratingsInfoComplaints: Complaints/recalls: lifetime counts reported to NHTSA for this vehicle — not part of the crash test itself.
safety.ratingsInfoInvestigations: Investigations: open or closed NHTSA safety investigations into this vehicle.

about.heading: About
about.body: This app shows vehicle data from the Ukrainian state open-data portal data.gov.ua, maintained by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Data is updated monthly.
about.vinBody: VIN decoding is done with the free NHTSA (USA) API.
